transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Dev Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (AtlasFin Head of Platform), Miguel Torres (AtlasFin SRE), Priya Singh (AtlasFin Product)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC check-in focused on rollout and go-live planning for AtlasFin pilot. Discussed canary strategy, A/B options, cutover plan, monitoring & runbooks, success criteria and security handoffs. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Canary vs A/B vs big-bang cutover
- Monitoring, alerts, and runbook steps (what to watch during canary)
- Traffic shaping and percent-based rollout
- Fallback/rollback thresholds and automated fallback policies
- Private deployment networking (VPC, KMS) and SOC2 deliverables
- Dry-run and benchmarking schedule

Transcript:
00:00 - Sophie: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. Laura, Miguel, Priya, we just wanted to do the usual weekly check-in — focus this week on the actual rollout plan. Hi Dev, hi team.
00:18 - Laura: Hi Sophie, thanks. Yes we want to lock the plan, especially cutover windows and who owns immediate rollbacks.
00:30 - Dev: Cool. I'll run through the proposed canary approach and monitoring. Quick note, apologies in advance, my connection might drop for a sec, AWS conference wifi is wild.
00:45 - Miguel: No worries. Our topline: we need sub-200ms p50 for the path that touches embeddings, and p95 under 600ms for generation. That's the internal target. If the pilot can't meet that we need to discuss dedicated vs hosted.
01:10 - Sophie: Got it. And to restate, the POC success criteria from last week were 1) latency SLOs 2) error rate <0.5% over 24h 3) functional correctness on the evaluation prompt set. Right?
01:25 - Priya: Yep, and add that product wants no regression on hallucination rate compared to baseline. We'll run the eval harness post-rollout.
01:40 - Dev: Alright, proposed canary plan: start with 1% of production traffic to Redwood Hosted endpoints for 4 hours, then 5% for 12 hours, 20% for 24 hours, then 50% for 24 hours, then full cutover. We recommend automated rollout with health checks on latency, error rate, and eval metric triggers.
02:05 - Miguel: For us 1% is good but who controls the routing? Is that on Redwood side or our side? We have an API gateway that can route based on header.
02:20 - Sophie: We can support both. Typically customers use their gateway to split traffic, but Redwood also supports policy-based routing and will do automated fallback to a baseline model variant if thresholds breach. We should decide which you prefer for this pilot.
02:38 - Laura: For security/audit reasons we prefer routing through our gateway so we retain full traffic logs. But we need Redwood to expose the canary health endpoints and a webhook for automated fallback.
02:50 - Dev: That's fine. We'll provide a health endpoint and webhook; Redwood will call back when the canary health crosses the threshold. There might be a slight delay in the rollback due to our gateway propagation time, so we'll include guardrails.
03:05 - Priya: Can you remind us of what metrics Redwood emits by default? We want to map them to our dashboards.
03:18 - Dev: Default telemetry includes token-level latency, request/response latency, model selection, GPU utilization, and model variant used. We also emit a per-route error code breakdown; sometimes the auto-transcript labels errors as 5xx or internal. We'll also add a custom event for evaluation checks.
03:36 - Miguel: We need minute-level granularity for alerts during canary — we don't want a 5-minute aggregation for p95.
03:45 - Sophie: Noted. We can expose 1m granularity via the console and a streaming metric sink to your Datadog. We'll include a recommended Datadog dashboard template in the runbook.
03:58 - Laura: On the security side, are we set for KMS integration? Our compliance team requires customer-managed keys.
04:10 - Sophie: Yes, for Redwood Private we support KMS/HSM. For Hosted we have envelope encryption, but if you need customer-managed keys you should be on the Private control plane. We can hand over the SOC2 + network diagram pack by tomorrow.
04:28 - Miguel: Great, can you include the audit log retention policy in that pack? We need 12 months.
04:36 - Sophie: Will do.
04:40 - Dev: Back to rollout, A/B was mentioned as an alternative. A/B is good for model comparison but complicates feature flags. For rollout safety, a canary + dark-launch A/B combination could let you compare hallucination/regression metrics without impacting real users.
05:00 - Priya: We like that idea — run the new model in shadow mode for 24h while the canary is live at 1-5% so we can compare outputs.
05:12 - Dev: Exactly. Shadow mode adds little latency to your system because Redwood can replicate requests asynchronously to the canary model. The transcript may say 'k v cache' sometimes — we support KV cache read-through to save generation cost.
05:28 - Miguel: On rollback thresholds: we propose stop + rollback if p95 > 800ms or error rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes, or any critical eval failure (hallucination rate jump > 20%). Thoughts?
05:45 - Sophie: Those are reasonable. From our experience, a 5-minute sustained breach is a good trigger, and we can add a soft-warning at 3 minutes to alert SREs. We should document exact thresholds in the runbook and make them configurable.
06:02 - Laura: For the cutover window, we were thinking a low-traffic period next Thursday 02:00-06:00 UTC. Does that work for Redwood?
06:12 - Dev: Works for us. We'll staff an engineer during that window; Sophie will be on call for escalation.
06:20 - Priya: One operational question: if we choose Dedicated GPUs later in pilot, does Redwood support live migration or do we need a separate cutover?
06:32 - Dev: Switching from Hosted to Dedicated is effectively a redeploy — model versions will be the same but the underlying runtime changes. We recommend a canary during the Dedicated provisioning too, so it's a 2-step process: canary on hosted, then canary on dedicated; you can avoid double cutover if you plan a single migration window but it's riskier.
06:55 - Miguel: Ok, we might start with Hosted canary to validate latency under real traffic and then provision Dedicated if we need consistent p95.
07:05 - Sophie: For monitoring and runbooks, we'll include: 1) pre-cutover checklist, 2) canary playbook with health endpoints and thresholds, 3) rollback steps and how to trigger automated fallback, 4) communications checklist (who to CC). We'll link to the runbook in the ticket.
07:20 - Laura: Can you also include an incident comms template and the exact PagerDuty routing keys we should use?
07:28 - Sophie: We'll include a template and sample PD integration steps. We won't store your PD keys — you'll configure that in the console.
07:36 - Priya: About metrics for eval/hallucination, will Redwood run evals in-band or do we need to pull logs?
07:48 - Dev: You can do either. For quick checks we can run evaluation prompts through the same endpoint and mark them; for continuous regression monitoring we recommend an async eval job that reads logs and scores responses. We'll provide the eval harness and a sample script.
08:05 - Miguel: For the dry-run, what load should we simulate? We want to make sure the autoscale and batching behave like production.
08:16 - Dev: If your target is 10k qps in production, start with a 10-20% staging load and step up. For the dry-run we can run a 10k qps burst for 10 minutes to validate tail latency and GPU utilization. We'll also validate KV cache hit ratios and batching efficiency.
08:36 - Sophie: We'll prepare a benchmark spreadsheet and share it; please annotate your real traffic distribution so our tuning suggestions (quantization profile, batch size) are aligned.
08:49 - Laura: Good — include cost estimates for Hosted vs Dedicated at each traffic band. We need to evaluate economics.
08:58 - Sophie: We'll include a cost model in the doc. It'll show per-token cost, amortized GPU cost on Dedicated, and break-even points.
09:08 - Miguel: One more security question — how do we handle logs that contain PII? We need redaction before logs leave our VPC.
09:18 - Dev: On Private we can run the control plane inside your VPC and logs never leave. For Hosted, we offer redact hooks and PII scrubbing; we'll document the options.
09:30 - Priya: Any outstanding blockers?
09:34 - Laura: SOC2 pack and runbook draft timeline is critical. Also we need the canary webhook test harness.
09:42 - Sophie: We'll send SOC2 + network pack by EOD 2026-11-18, and the canary webhook test harness alongside the runbook draft on 2026-11-19.
09:52 - Miguel: I'll confirm precise SLO numbers and the percent of traffic for each canary step by 2026-11-20.
10:00 - Dev: I'll scope the dry-run script and share the benchmark plan; aim to run the dry-run on 2026-11-24, we'll coordinate time zones.
10:12 - Sophie: Great. Quick note — in case of auto fallback, Redwood can return to the baseline model variant or route traffic to a multi-tenant fallback pool. We'll include decision guidance in runbook.
10:27 - Priya: What about canary duration for A/B compare? We want 24-48h of shadow traffic to get statistically significant hallucination metrics.
10:38 - Dev: Agreed. For hallucination you need a larger sample size so plan for 48h of shadow + 24h of increased canary traffic if you can.
10:52 - Laura: Ok that aligns with our product team.
11:00 - Sophie: Any final questions?
11:05 - Miguel: One more — who will run the post-rollout retro? We want a blameless postmortem template.
11:12 - Sophie: We'll provide a template and propose Redwood and AtlasFin co-own the retro.
11:20 - Priya: Sounds good.
11:25 - Sophie: Alright, I'll recap next steps.
11:30 - Sophie (recap): 1) Send SOC2/network pack and audit retention info by 2026-11-18. 2) Share canary runbook and webhook harness by 2026-11-19. 3) Miguel to share SLOs and traffic percents by 2026-11-20. 4) Dev + Miguel dry-run 2026-11-24. 5) Post-rollout retro template in runbook.
11:58 - Laura: Thanks everyone. This was helpful.
12:05 - Sophie: Thanks all, talk soon.

End of meeting.
